title: Categories of ecosystem services

definition.text: The four-way grouping of nature's benefits into provisioning, regulating, supporting and cultural services, set out by the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment.

facts.text: Provisioning services are the products obtained from ecosystems, such as food, fresh water, wood, fibre and fuel.
Regulating services are benefits from the regulation of ecosystem processes, such as climate control, carbon sequestration, flood control and disease regulation.
Supporting services, such as nutrient cycling, primary production and soil formation, allow the other services to exist.
Cultural services include recreation, tourism and spiritual gratification.
To avoid double-counting, The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity replaced supporting services with habitat services.
The Common International Classification of Ecosystem Services was built for accounting systems such as national accounts, again to avoid double-counting.

title: Nature's Services (1997)

definition.text: Gretchen Daily's edited book Nature's Services: Societal Dependence on Natural Ecosystems, published in 1997, which laid out the framework widely used for understanding nature's benefits to people.

facts.text: It opens with Daily's introduction 'What are Ecosystem Services' and a history of the idea by Harold Mooney and Paul Ehrlich.
It and Costanza and colleagues' global valuation were the two seminal 1990s works on ecosystem services.
It served as a model for ecosystem regulation in several regions and was a catalyst for the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment.
